name: Albedo Shard
description: Albedo Shard is a small, airless world of extraordinary reflectivity, its crystalline surface bouncing back nearly all incident light in a dazzling display that makes the planet visible to the naked eye from neighboring worlds. The surface is composed of tightly packed silicon crystals interlaced with metallic deposits, polished by micrometeorite bombardment over billions of years into a near-perfect mirror. Impact crater chains scar this reflective surface in long arcs, their darker interiors exposing the metallic core fragments beneath.

Without atmosphere, the planet's surface alternates between searing heat in direct starlight and bitter cold in shadow. The transition is immediate and total, with temperature swings of three hundred degrees occurring across the shadow line. The brilliance of the sunlit surface is intense enough to damage optical sensors at close range, requiring filtered observation from orbit.

The planet appears to be a fragment of a larger body, its exposed core materials and irregular shape suggesting a catastrophic collision in the distant past. The crystalline surface layer may be the remnant of a once-deeper geological formation, now exposed and polished by eons of cosmic weathering. The impact crater chains align in patterns suggesting a secondary bombardment event, possibly from debris of the same collision that created the shard.

Albedo Shard's platinum deposits are unusually pure and accessible, concentrated in the exposed core fragments where geological processing has separated the metal from surrounding rock. The mining challenge is primarily operational: the blinding surface reflectivity, extreme temperature swings, and low gravity create a hostile environment for both human and robotic workers. A proposed orbital processing facility would use focused sunlight reflected from the planet's own surface to refine extracted ores.
